## Why the review looks like this
Explain cheapest candidate is the half‑precision candidate to validate first because it uses least energy per inference and lowest latency though it draws more power while running than the eight‑bit builds.  
The position fine‑tune (same half‑precision engine cost) removed the start‑position weakness shown at both held‑out shifts giving clear improvement but it has not yet shown nominal performance at the training mark because the comparison there is undecided.  
Success comparisons against full precision cannot be decided yet because the confidence intervals for each candidate cross the ten‑point tolerance band leaving the evidence insufficient.  
The deliberately miscalibrated builds are stopped at the simple input check because that check catches the bad calibration before any other test runs.  
The AI judge’s record shows it is wording‑sensitive looks only at the final state gives more false alarms on novel objects so it must be re‑validated before trust it cleared re‑check on fresh live trials in the fine‑tune study but still needs checking on other objects and scenes.  

## Questions to resolve before deployment
- How many trials are needed to shrink the confidence interval so the lower bound stays above minus ten points for each candidate?  
- Does the half‑precision candidate meet the power budget when measured under sustained load?  
- Does the position fine‑tune maintain nominal performance at the training mark when tested with more repetitions?  
- Can the AI judge be relied on for unseen objects after additional validation on varied scenes?  
- Are there any hidden failure modes in the stress scenarios that require extra probing?
